info.name: Wikimedia Enterprise APIs
info.description: # Quick Links - [Wikimedia Enterprise APIs overview](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/) - [Reference Documentation](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/) - [OpenAPI definition (YAML)](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/wme-api.yaml) - [Data Schema Explanation: Data Dictionary](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/data-dictionary/) - [Best Practices](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/best-practices/) **Disclaimer: this Postman Collection is not meant as complete reference documentation. It is meant to be used for endpoint discovery and testing purposes. It describes the most-used endpoints and methods, but it does not exhaustively list every endpoint and method. For complete refdocs, please visit** [enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/) # Using this collection 1. **Create an account.** [Sign up for a free account](https://dashboard.enterprise.wikimedia.com/signup/) and verify your email. 2. **Store your credentials in the Postman Vault.** Click **Vault** in the footer at the bottom of the Postman window. The first time, Postman asks you to create a vault key, a password that protects the vault on this computer: keep **Save this key to native password manager** ticked so you aren't asked for it again, and keep a copy in your password manager. Then, in your local vault, click **Add new secret** and create two secrets: - `wmeUsername`: your Wikimedia Enterprise username, in lowercase - `wmePassword`: your Wikimedia Enterprise password In **Allowed domains**, enter `https://auth.enterprise.wikimedia.com` for both secrets. That's the only place the collection sends your credentials, and Postman won't use them for any other site. 3. **Let the collection read the vault.** In the vault, click the settings icon at the top right, turn on **Allow Vault secrets in scripts**. 4. **Send a request.** Open **On-demand > Article Lookup**. In the request URL, hover over `{{articlename}}` and type `NASA` in the box that appears. Click **Send**. The first time, Postman asks "Grant Vault access for this execution?": keep **Only this collection** selected and click **Grant Access**. The collection logs in for you and the request returns the article. You don't need to run **Authentication > Login** yourself or set up an environment. The collection logs in before your first request, keeps your tokens in collection variables, and refreshes the access token before it expires. **If a request fails:** - **"Wikimedia Enterprise credentials not found":** check that both secrets exist with exactly those names (step 2) and that **Allow Vault secrets in scripts** is on (step 3). - **You chose Deny Access by mistake:** in the vault, open **Settings**, then the **Manage access** tab, and click **Grant Access** next to the collection. - **401 Unauthorized:** check your username and password in the vault. The Postman Console (at the bottom of the window) shows each login and refresh. # Introduction Wikimedia Enterprise is a [suite of APIs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/) designed for **high-volume read-only access to Wikipedia and other** [supported Wikimedia projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/). These APIs have been developed and are maintained by the Wikimedia Foundation. All endpoints return data in a consistent schema, so you can combine articles from Snapshot, On-demand, or Realtime without creating separate parsers. Our Snapshot and Realtime: Batch endpoints return tar.gz files and an NDJSON header. All other API endpoints return JSON by default. Read our [Data Primer](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/about/data-primer/) to understand how data from Wikimedia projects is created and maintained. With Wikimedia Enterprise APIs, you can: - **Download an entire Wikimedia project** (HTML Database Dump) - Call the [Snapshot API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/) to receive a binary data file (compressed into a .tar.gz file) containing every single article in a specific project, e.g. all of English Wikipedia or German Wiktionary. - **Request the latest public version of a single article**: - Query the [On-demand API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/) by article name, like "Albert_Einstein" or "SpaceX", to receive the most recent article version in all projects. You can also use filters for language and/or project of choice. - **Stream real-time updates** (firehose) from [supported projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/): - Connect to the [Realtime API stream](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/) to have all article revisions (updates) pushed directly to your system as they happen. - Use [Realtime: Batch](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/) to download new updates in a tarball (.tar.gz). These are updated on the hour with the last day of updates available. # First Step: Sign Up _Note: if you are a Wikimedia community member, you can get exclusive access to Wikimedia Enterprise APIs. Find out more_ [here](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Enterprise#Access)_._ To get started, [sign up for a free account](https://dashboard.enterprise.wikimedia.com/signup/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=signup&utm_content=docs-start) (_no credit card required_), verify your email, then follow the next steps on this page. # Getting your access tokens Now that you've set up and verified your account, send the **username** (_all lowercase_)**and password you created** to the [/login endpoint](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/) to receive your tokens. Wikimedia Enterprise **APIs use JWT authentication passed in the header** for access verification. All API requests must be made over HTTPS and must pass that Bearer access token in the header; without it the requests will fail. ``` curl -L https://auth.enterprise.wikimedia.com/v1/login -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"username":"yourusername", "password":"secret"}' ``` Refresh tokens expire in 90 days. Access and ID tokens expire in 24 hours. Use your Refresh token to obtain a new Access token before it expires. _An important reminder: Your credentials carry many privileges related to your account, so be careful to keep them secure. Do not share your credentials in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, etc._ # Make your first API Calls Now you are ready to make your first call. Start by running this cURL command, with your access token in the `ACCESS_TOKEN` shell variable (`export ACCESS_TOKEN=...`). You'll receive a list of all [supported projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/) available to you in our APIs, including the project name, identifier, language, and more. _**Note:**_ the project identifier (e.g. "`enwiki`" for English Wikipedia) is the identifier you will use to identify the project and language in requests. ``` bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -L https://api.enterprise.wikimedia.com/v2/projects ``` Next, try using the [Snapshot API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/). Run this cURL command to download a compressed file (_HTML dump_) containing every article in English Wikipedia (_it's large_). _**Note:**_ _the "Snapshot identifier" is constructed with 3 items from our_ [metadata endpoints](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)_: <_[language](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)_\><_[project_name](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)_\>_namespace_<[number](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)__>_ Uncompress that file to see NDJSON with each line representing a single article in the project. An [example of an article's payload](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/) can be seen on our API page, and to learn more about each field in the payload, see our [data dictionary](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/data-dictionary/). ``` bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" -L https://api.enterprise.wikimedia.com/v2/snapshots/enwiki_namespace_0/download --output enwiki.tar.gz ``` Next, try calling the [On-demand API](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/#article-lookup) to get single article (page) of interest. Let's use NASA in English Wikipedia as an example, with this cURL command. ``` bash curl -X 'POST' \ 'https://api.enterprise.wikimedia.com/v2/articles/NASA' \ -H 'accept: application/json' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "filters": [ { "field": "is_part_of.identifier", "value": "enwiki" } ], "limit": 1 }' ``` You'll receive a JSON response containing the same article data and format represented in the Snapshot API's file. The main difference here (_besides being able to query pages individually_) is that this response returns the live version of the article that is actively on the project today, whereas snapshots update daily with a paid account or monthly with a free account. # **Software Development Kits (SDKs)** [Go SDK](https://github.com/wikimedia-enterprise/wme-sdk-go) [Python SDK](https://github.com/wikimedia-enterprise/wme-sdk-python) # **Next Steps** You've created your account and made your first calls to Wikimedia Enterprise. - Choose which [Wikimedia Enterprise APIs](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/) fit your use case and start making some requests. - The [data dictionary](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/data-dictionary/) explains our schema and response fields. - Import the [OpenAPI definition YAML file](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/wme-api.yaml) into your favorite API discovery platform. - The [Best Practices](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/best-practices/) page describes optimal ways of using the Wikimedia Enterprise APIs. If you have some additional questions, look through the [FAQs](https://helpcenter.enterprise.wikimedia.com/) or use [your account dashboard](https://dashboard.enterprise.wikimedia.com/) to contact support or provide feedback. Wikimedia Enterprise operates a status page at [status.enterprise.wikimedia.com](https://status.enterprise.wikimedia.com/) displaying uptime history and current status. If you are interested in daily Snapshot dumps, Realtime firehose, or additional egress, [contact us](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/contact/).

item.description: Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/) Use your account credentials (_username in lowercase_) and tokens to manage your account programmatically. Access tokens expire after 24 hours, while refresh tokens expire after 90 days. You can only use the same refresh token up to 90 times to get a new access token. Use the [Login](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/) endpoint to receive your tokens, then use the [Refresh Token](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/) and [Revoke Token](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/authentication/) endpoints to manage them. Your account password can also be managed with the associated endpoints referenced in this document. _Note: if you are a Wikimedia community member, you can get exclusive access to Wikimedia Enterprise APIs that might not need authentication. Find out more_ [here](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Enterprise#Access)_._

Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/)

Metadata endpoints provide the reference data you'll need to use the APIs effectively. These utility endpoints return project codes, language identifiers, and namespace mappings. See: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/structured-contents/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/api/structured-contents/)

Structured Contents extracts infoboxes, sections, tables, references, and more from raw wikitext and HTML and delivers them as structured, machine-readable JSON.

Structured Contents currently extracts the following article pieces into JSON:

- `abstract`
    
- `description`
    
- `main image`
    
- `infobox`
    
- `sections`
    
- `lists`
    
- `citations` & `references`
    
- `tables`

item.description:
Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/snapshot/)

Our Snapshot API provides you the entirety of a Wikimedia project (examples: English Wikipedia or French Wiktionary) in a compressed tarball (.tar.gz) that contains a single .ndjson file. This file holds all articles (pages), with all data fields, in Newline-Delimited JSON format. **Updated once a month, on the 1st day of the month**, these snapshots are **provided free** with an account. A free account also includes Structured Contents snapshots.

Use our [metadata endpoints](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/) to find the project snapshot(s) you need and make use of parallel downloading headers or chunking to break up large files. Feel free to reference our [Data Dictionary](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/data-dictionary/) for information about the fields in the payload.

If you need fresher data, you can get up to daily snapshot updates by [contacting Sales](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/contact/).

_Note: Snapshots, Structured Contents snapshots, and chunks may contain a small amount of duplicate articles (< 1%). Similarly, they may contain a small amount of deleted articles.__When encountering more than one instance of an article, please use the one with the highest version.identifier number. This will be the latest among the duplicates.__When encountering deleted articles, please download the successive snapshots. The deleted articles will be removed in the successive generation of these snapshots, Structured Contents snapshots, and chunks._

item.name: On-demand
Wikidata On-demand

request.description:
Returns data and metadata about the last revision of a given Wikidata Item identifier (Q-number, e.g. Q42). Only gives access to the Main Wikidata graph.

Required: `{{wikidata_item_id}}`, a Q-number (e.g., Q42: Douglas Adams)

Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/items/{identifier}](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/items/{identifier})

Returns data and metadata about the last revision of a given Wikidata Property identifier (P-number, e.g. P31).

Required: `{{wikidata_property_id}}`, a P-number (e.g., P106: occupation)

Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/properties/{identifier}](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/properties/{identifier})

Returns a single JSON object of key-value pairs, where the key is the Wikimedia language code and the value is the label for that language code. Works for Wikidata item identifiers (Q-number) and property identifiers (P-number). Only gives access to the Main Wikidata graph for item identifiers. Gives access to all property identifiers.

Required: `{{wikidata_entity_id}}`, a Q- or P-number

Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/labels/{identifier}](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/api/#tag/wikidata/POST/v2/wikidata/labels/{identifier})

item.description:
Reference Documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/#wikidata-item-lookup-beta](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/#wikidata-item-lookup-beta)

Wikidata is the central knowledge base for the structured data of Wikimedia's projects: Wikipedia, Wikivoyage, Wiktionary, and more. It connects data from disparate Wikimedia projects and languages, as well as hundreds of external databases and knowledge bases, through their identifiers. In this way, Wikidata is a hub of linked knowledge. It currently contains over 120 million items, structured as Linked Open Data.

| Endpoint Name | Primary Purpose | Required identifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Item Lookup | Get all data and metadata of the last revision of an item: revision info, labels, descriptions, statements, sitelinks | Q-number (e.g., Q42: Douglas Adams) |
| Property Lookup | Retrieve all information about a property, a single category that connects statements | P-number (e.g., P106: occupation) |

item.description:
Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand)

Our On-demand REST API returns the current version of any article from all [supported Wikimedia projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/). Query by article name across all projects or use [metadata filtering](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/metadata/) to request by project and language, with more options to optimize response payloads. On-demand returns JSON by default, but if you would prefer an NDJSON response be sure to include the `Accept: application/x-ndjson` header in your requests.

The [Structured Contents articles endpoint](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/on-demand/) is our sandbox beta endpoint that includes fully parsed Wikipedia Infobox and article sections data in JSON.

Reference documentation: [https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/docs/realtime/)

Receive real-time event updates from all [supported Wikimedia projects](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/project-data/) using the streaming (firehose) endpoint, or via batch file endpoints that are generated hourly with changes throughout the day.

Streaming supports server-sent events (SSE) by default or NDJSON when you pass the `Accept: application/x-ndjson` header. Batch files return NDJSON in a tarball (.tar.gz).

Event types are: update, delete, visibility-change:

- An `update` event type is sent when an article is created, its content is updated, or its name or namespace is changed.
    
- A `delete` event type is sent when an article has been deleted.
    
- A `visibility-change` event type is sent when the visibility of an article's editor, comment, or content is changed by community volunteers
    

For access to Realtime endpoints, [contact our sales team](https://enterprise.wikimedia.com/contact/).

exec: * Wikimedia Enterprise APIs: automatic login and token refresh.
* Runs before every request except those sent to the auth server (the Authentication folder).
* It logs in when there is no token, refreshes the access token an hour before it expires, and
* logs in again when the refresh token is near its 90-day limit or a refresh fails.
*  1. Add your Wikimedia Enterprise username and password to your Postman Vault as the secrets
*  2. Let scripts read the vault: in the Vault, open Settings and turn on "Allow Vault secrets
*     in scripts". If Postman asks, allow this collection.
* Tokens and their expiry times are kept in collection variables, so no environment is needed.
* Outside the Postman app (Newman, Postman CLI), pass wmeUsername and wmePassword as environment
? `Postman did not let this script read the vault (${vaultError}). In the vault, open Settings and turn on "Allow Vault secrets in scripts".`
: "Add wmeUsername and wmePassword to your Postman Vault, spelled exactly like that.";
throw new Error(`Wikimedia Enterprise credentials not found. ${reason} See the collection overview.`);
const response = await send("/v1/login", { username, password });
throw new Error(`Login failed with HTTP ${response.code}. Check the wmeUsername and wmePassword vault secrets.`);
const response = await send("/v1/token-refresh", { username, refresh_token: refreshToken });
console.warn(`Token refresh failed with HTTP ${response.code}; logging in again.`);
// Earlier versions of this collection kept tokens in the active environment, where they would
// override the collection variables this script now uses.
console.log("Removed token variables left in the environment by an earlier version of this collection.");
